svg.desc: Banner for a paper refuting the affine Karpelevich conjecture for Markov rate matrices. Left: the Karpelevich region Omega_4, the set of all eigenvalues of four-by-four stochastic matrices, drawn exactly inside the dashed unit circle. Its boundary runs straight from 1 to i, along a curved arc from i to e^{2 pi i/3}, and along a curved arc from e^{2 pi i/3} to -1 (highlighted), with the mirror image below. A small box marks the window magnified on the right. Right: the magnified window near the left arc, using the exact boundary formula from the paper. The region inside Omega_4 is shaded below the arc. The rescaled eigenvalue zeta of the paper’s integer four-state rate matrix, approximately -0.7062 + 0.3161 i, sits 0.0087 above the arc, outside the region, whereas the conjecture requires it to lie inside.
svg.text: One eigenvalue escapes the squashed Karpelevich region
A driven four-state network whose rescaled eigenvalue lies just outside Ω₄, refuting the affine Karpelevich conjecture
Ω₄: all eigenvalues of 4×4 stochastic matrices
rescaled eigenvalue ζ of the four-state witness
ζ ≈ −0.7062 + 0.3161 i; conjecture (S3) needs ζ in Ω₄
boundary arc of Ω₄ (from −1 to e^(2πi/3))
exact boundary curve y = √g(x) (Lemma 2.6) · real part horizontal, imaginary part vertical · magnified window
